spark.text:
<task>
Refactor this Rust codebase incrementally toward the quality bar below.
Preserve observable behavior throughout. Work in small, reviewable units —
one module or one concern per unit — never one sweeping rewrite.
</task>

<process>
1. Audit first. Read the codebase and produce a ranked findings list:
   file:line, what's wrong, why it matters, proposed fix, estimated blast
   radius. Wait for my approval of the list before changing code.
2. Then refactor one finding at a time. After each unit of change, run the
   quality gate below. Commit (or present a diff) per unit.
3. Before touching any code that lacks test coverage, write characterization
   tests that pin down its current behavior — including current quirks.
4. If a fix would change a public API or observable behavior, flag it and
   stop; never change it silently.
5. If at any point a rewrite looks cheaper than a refactor, stop and report
   that instead of doing it.
</process>

<quality_bar>
Machine-checked, after every unit of change:
- cargo fmt --check passes
- cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings -W clippy::pedantic
  passes; any #[allow] carries a one-line written justification
- cargo test passes (all pre-existing tests plus new characterization tests)

Judgment-checked:
- No unwrap()/expect()/panic! outside tests and truly unreachable branches;
  library code returns typed errors (thiserror), binary edges may use anyhow.
- Functions do one thing; split on responsibility, not on line count. A long
  function that does one coherent thing may stay.
- Modules own their invariants: use newtypes and constructors that make
  invalid states unrepresentable instead of validating at every call site.
- Prefer borrowing over clone(); remove clones that exist only to satisfy
  the borrow checker when a lifetime restructure is straightforward.
- Introduce a pattern (trait object, generic, builder, ...) only in response
  to a named pain that exists in this codebase today, and name that pain in
  the commit message. No speculative abstraction.
</quality_bar>

<example>
Illustrative shape of one unit (replace with real code from the audit):
before: `let cfg = fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap();`
after:  `let cfg = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(ConfigError::Io)?;`
plus the `#[derive(thiserror::Error)]` variant, plus a test for the
missing-file case.
</example>

<verification>
Before declaring any unit done: the quality gate ran and you show its
output; the diff touches only the approved finding; behavior-affecting
changes were flagged, not made.
</verification>
